title: Scene
description: The single primitive of the Yunyou engine. A tour = ordered/branching list of scenes. Every product (guided tour, photo album, course) is authored content on this runtime.

type.description: See studio/research/scene-types.md for the catalogue; panorama/window/ambience/drone/timeline are research-track types.

subtopic.description: The rundown subtopic this scene realises

learning_goal.description: One sentence: what the traveller should know/feel afterwards

script.description: Spoken script. Plain text, no stage directions. ~150 wpm.

timing.description: When speech plays relative to the interaction: before / over (default) / after. For scenes that pause on an interaction, put the sentences that must come AFTER the answer in after_script instead.

after_script.description: Spoken after the interaction resolves (answer chosen, walk finished, chat handed back, timeout hit). Plain text like script. Counted in the words-per-second rule.

starts_at_s.description: Seconds into the scene when speech begins (default 0). The validator measures words-per-second over duration_s - starts_at_s.

variants.description: Parallel narration tracks keyed by variant id; each value is a full replacement for `script` (plain text, same rules and w/s budget). Current ids: "clear" = simplified plain-English track for non-native speakers, selected on the player start screen (TTS slows to 0.9 unless the traveller picked a speed). Missing variant → the player falls back to `script`. Future ids: language codes (zh, …).

after_script_variants.description: Same variant ids as `variants`, but for `after_script`: a full replacement for the post-interaction line so the chosen track does not change register mid-scene (fact-check A5, 2026-08-19). Missing id → the runtime falls back to `after_script`. Not counted twice by the validator: the w/s budget still measures `after_script` once per track. The walk key `waypoint_script` has the same twin, `waypoint_script_variants` (object of variant id → array of blocks, one per route index; `variants.<id>` must be their join).

ref.description: YouTube video id, URL, file path (for kind 'footage': path relative to the chapter dir, e.g. media/files/x.mp4), or 'lat,lng,heading,pitch,fov'

license.description: e.g. youtube-embed, cc-by-4.0, public-domain, generated, licensed

fallback.description: Manifest id (M-xx) or ref shown if this media cannot load (no Maps JS key, deleted video, offline). For streetview stops: the still to show instead of the pano.

note.description: Free note for the Scene Developer / renderer (framing, crop, why this clip). Not shown to the traveller.

use.description: Where this entry may be used. 'player' = interactive player only (e.g. a YouTube embed we may show but not copy); 'linear' = rendered MP4 only (e.g. our self-hosted cut of the same shot); 'both' (default) = either. Added 2026-08-19 (A8) so a scene can record the embed AND the local file for the same shot.

audio.description: How the renderer must treat this item's own audio. Default for kind 'footage' with an archive/PD source is 'mute' (uploader-added soundtracks over public-domain film are not licensed to us).

sa.description: True if this item is derived from CC BY-SA material — the strip-list flag from review/rights-a6.md §2.4.

treatment.description: kind 'image' only. How the player presents a still that does not fill the frame. Omit and the player decides from the file's real pixels and the real frame — that is the right answer nearly always. 'backdrop' = fill the bars with a blurred, darkened copy of this same picture; 'plate' = mount it on warm paper with a caption line (small period engravings, elevations, plans); 'fill' = plain contain, no backdrop; 'none' = opt out of the treatment layer entirely (black bars, no motion). Nothing is ever stretched, upscaled past the file's own pixels or cropped, whichever is chosen. Added v0.7 (player); scenes without the key are unaffected.

drift.description: kind 'image' only. false = this still does not drift. Use for a beat that must sit still (a held silence, a portrait, a death). Prefer this over treatment:'none', which also removes the backdrop and leaves black bars. Added v0.9.

overlays.description: Timed layers on top of media, synced to scene time (seconds from scene start) or, in walks, to waypoints (at_waypoint).

at_s.description: Seconds from scene start. Always required: it is the linear/no-JS fallback even when at_waypoint is set.

at_waypoint.description: Index into interaction.route: show this overlay when the walk reaches that waypoint (interactive runtime). at_s remains the linear fallback. Overlays with at_waypoint are exempt from the ~1-per-15-s density rule.

kind.description: gloss = glossary chip for a period/hard word: text is 'word — plain-English definition' (em-dash separator); the player renders a tappable 📖 chip and speaks the definition on tap. Gloss overlays are exempt from the ~1-per-15-s density rule.
save = card scenes: traveller keeps the card (souvenir/recipe) — runtime offers download/share; no answer required.

pause_narration.description: Runtime holds narration and the scene clock at the interaction until it resolves or timeout_s elapses. Requires timeout_s. Sentences after the answer go in narration.after_script.

timeout_s.description: Honest budget for the wait state: seconds the runtime waits for the traveller before auto-resolving (skip / reveal / hand back). Per tap for tap-to-find. Also the number the length budget uses.

guardrails.description: dialogue: what the persona must not claim

on_llm_unavailable.description: dialogue: what the runtime does without an LLM/API key. choice = show options[] as chips with their feedback as scripted answers; skip = play narration and move on; scripted = play a canned exchange from options[] in order.

max_exchanges.description: dialogue: free exchanges allowed before the persona hands back (after_script). Budget = max_exchanges within timeout_s.

route.description: streetview walk: waypoints 'lat,lng' or 'lat,lng,heading[,pitch[,fov]]'. overlays[].at_waypoint indexes into this list.

camera.description: streetview: timed look-at cues for the cinematic auto-walk (player v0.4). The camera walks the route by itself, paced to duration_s, and turns to whatever a cue names, easing in and out — it never snaps. Between cues it looks along the direction of travel. Keep at_s equal to the at_s of the overlay/pin that names the same thing, so the pin and the turn coincide. Ignored by scenes of other types and by the linear renderer.

at_s.description: Seconds from scene start when the turn begins.

heading.description: Compass heading to look at (0 = north, 90 = east). Required unless look_at is given; also the fallback for modes that cannot compute a bearing.

look_at.description: 'lat,lng' of the thing to look at. Preferred over heading: the runtime computes the bearing from wherever the camera actually is, so the framing survives Google moving the nearest pano.

pitch.description: Up/down angle (default 0). Positive looks up — use it for towers, spires and façades seen from close by.

zoom.description: Street View zoom; fov = 180 / 2^zoom (0 = 180°, 0.85 = the walking default ≈ 100°, 1 = 90°, 2 = 45°).

hold_s.description: Seconds to hold this framing before the walk moves on. The camera stops walking while it looks.

ease_s.description: Seconds the turn takes (default 1.8). Long turns for reveals, short for glances; 0 still eases, it never cuts.

at_waypoint.description: Index into interaction.route this cue belongs to — documentation for reviewers and a validator cross-check; the runtime paces from at_s.

label.description: What we are looking at, e.g. 'Reform Club façade, 104 Pall Mall'. Reviewer note, never shown to the traveller.

next.description: Default next scene id; branches override via interaction.options[].goto

sources.description: Fact-sheet ids backing every claim in the narration/quiz (F-01, F-02…)
